hints.content:
First, we see that the relationship *is* proportional.  The point $(\pink0,\blue0)$ is in the table, and for each increase of $3$ in $x$, there is an increase of $0.6$ in $y$.  Let’s find the unit rate of change of $y$ with respect to $x$: what is the $y$-value corresponding to $x=\pink1?$

$\begin{align}\dfrac{\blue{0.6}}{\pink{3}}&=\dfrac{\blue{\dfrac{3}{5}}}{{\pink3}}\\ &\\&\\&\\
&=\blue{\dfrac{3}{5}}\cdot\pink{\dfrac{1}{3}}\\&\\&=\dfrac{1}{5}=0.2\end{align}$ 

 This is the unit rate, and the point $\left(\pink1,\blue{\dfrac{1}{5}}\right)$ lies on the line.  However, to graph the line representing the relationship, it will be helpful to find another point on the line.

The graph goes through $(\pink0,\blue0)$.   Because the unit rate is $\dfrac{1}{5}$ , a change of $\pink{5}$ units in $x$ results in an increase of $\dfrac{1}{5}(\pink{5})=\blue{1}$ unit in $y$.  So the point $(\pink{5},\blue{{1}})$  lies on the graph.    Now we can draw the line connecting these two points.

![](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/80243290e1b7fa2ab2400e9ff02659e9e7c0f8c8)

Since the graph goes through $(\pink0,\blue0)$ and $(\pink5,\blue{1})$, 
 the slope is

$\dfrac{\left(\blue{1}-\blue0\right)}{(\pink5-\pink0)}=\dfrac{1}{5}$ , the same as the unit rate of change of $y$ with respect to $x$.
